source_documents.title: Facilitating J-Aggregate Formation by Lowering Activation Energy to Achieve Ultrahigh Brightness for NIR-II Fluorescence Imaging and Photoacoustic Imaging

reference_evidence_units.quote: Among them compound ABS with substituents of dibenzothiophene exhibited the strongest J-aggregation propensity, as evidenced by aggregation kinetics studies.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ABS, ABO, ABN

reference_evidence_units.quote: ABN and ABS form antiparallel slip-stacked J-dimer (Figure 2a) and the slipping angles are measured to be 35.2° and 30.5°, respectively, which conforms to the characteristics of Jaggregates (θ < 54.7°).
reference_evidence_units.subject: ABS
reference_evidence_units.statement: J-type slip-stacked dimers in the crystal.

reference_evidence_units.quote: ABO exhibited well-ordered antiparallel slip-stacked with slip angle of 31.5°.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ABO

reference_evidence_units.quote: Meanwhile, a new J band emerged at around 852 nm.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ABS
reference_evidence_units.statement: Metastable aggregates convert to J-aggregates (Ea 74 kJ/mol).

reference_evidence_units.quote: Concurrently, the emission intensity also increased constantly when excited at 852 nm.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ABS
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emission grows with the J band.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The activation energy was calculated to be 91 kJ/mol, which was higher than that of ABS (Figure S2b,c).
reference_evidence_units.subject: ABO
reference_evidence_units.statement: ABO forms a J band at 824 nm, more slowly.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This molecular engineering strategy promoted exciton delocalization and accelerated radiative decay (kr = 0.191 ns−1) for NIR-II J-aggregates of ABS-2 in water, achieving a record-high absolute quantum yield of 10.11%.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ABS-2
reference_evidence_units.statement: J-aggregation raises kr and gives Φ 10.1% in the NIR-II.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These assemblies exhibited classical J-type characteristics: narrowed absorption and emission bandwidths, minimized Stokes shifts, enhanced extinction coefficient and radiative decay rate.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ABS-1, ABS-2

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Side chains promote ordered J-aggregates in water with the classic J signatures; record NIR-II Φ 10.1%.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The brightness gain is explained by a faster radiative rate of the J-aggregate (exciton delocalisation).

contrast_group.varied_factor: relative to ABS: dibenzofuran instead of dibenzothiophene (ABO), or amphiphilic side chains (ABS-2)
contrast_group.paper_difference: ABS forms J-aggregates in water with the lowest barrier; ABO needs more activation; the side chains of ABS-2 give ordered J-aggregates with high kr and Φ.
